text:
Hey man, really good educational video and definitely exciting, but I think one important thing gets blurred here, automation intelligence and trading edge are not the same thing.
An AI can research, monitor, schedule tasks and place trades, but you still need a real buy/sell strategy that actually has an edge. You also probably won't get fast, reliable news just by searching in the morning and build a strategy around that.
The risky implication is that a smart model can just figure out how to trade profitably across different market conditions. I don't think we're there yet.
I've been building my own trading software, and connecting AI to a broker is honestly the easy part. Strategy, market data, execution, risk, position truth and validation are where most of the work is.
Very powerful idea, but to me this is more like 20% of the full problem.

text:
Really interesting setup. I’m building something very similar with Astra/Alpaca, but I ran into OpenAI’s safety restrictions once we got to autonomous execution.

OpenAI’s published agent policy specifically says users shouldn’t “automate actions like stock trading or other investment transactions.” From what I can tell in this video, Astra has built the strategy, connected to the live Alpaca account, and scheduled the trading routines—but the first actual live trades haven’t happened yet.

Have you tested whether Astra will actually submit a real-money order autonomously when one of these routines fires? If so, how are you handling that policy restriction? Are you expecting Astra to place the trades directly, or is there some human-approval/execution step that wasn’t shown in the video?

Very curious because this is exactly where our implementation hit the safety boundary.
